paragraphs: This career is a poor fit for people who dislike dirt or physical work and lack patience. Daily tasks involve grease, corrosion, and burned coils. Cleaning parts in cold water during winter is also common. Impatience can ruin precise work.
Remember: the goal is to restore equipment to factory condition. Winding tension, bearing alignment, and complete testing directly determine how many more years a machine can run.

This career is a poor fit for people who dislike dirt or physical work and lack patience. Daily tasks involve grease, corrosion, and burned coils. Cleaning parts in cold water during winter is also common. Impatience can ruin precise work.

A common path is: study electromechanical systems or electrical repair at a technical or vocational school; apprentice in a repair shop or factory equipment department; earn an electrician license and occupational credentials while working; specialize in motors, tools, or variable-frequency drives; then open a repair shop or provide on-site factory maintenance.

This career suits practical, patient, exacting people. Dismantling a motor requires remembering the relative position of hundreds of parts and reassembling every one correctly. Testing combines sound, sparks, and current readings, so careless workers struggle.

Electric Motor, Power Tool, And Related Repairers diagnose, dismantle, repair, and test motors, generators, power tools, and similar electrical equipment. They replace coils, bearings, brushes, and other parts, then perform balancing, insulation, and operating tests.

entries: Electric Motor, Power Tool, And Related Repairers diagnose, dismantle, repair, and test motors, generators, power tools, and similar electrical equipment. They replace coils, bearings, brushes, and other parts, then perform balancing, insulation, and operating tests.
Diagnose electrical and mechanical faults in motors, power tools, and related equipment.
Dismantle equipment and replace windings, bearings, brushes, switches, and other parts.
Wind motor coils and perform insulation and dielectric-strength tests.
Balance rotors dynamically, adjust clearances, and assemble equipment.
Run no-load and load tests, measure current, listen for unusual sounds, and check temperature rise.
Maintain repair records and recommend maintenance or replacement.

paragraphs: Work pace follows orders. During slow periods, technicians repair small tools and sort inventory. Factory maintenance and seasonal demand can create evening overtime. One technician often handles inspection, dismantling, estimates, repair, testing, and delivery. Repaired equipment receives a test label, and technicians explain operating precautions to customers on site.

In one sentence: diagnose, dismantle, repair, replace parts, and test. Tasks include inspecting motors, replacing windings, bearings, and brushes, winding coils, testing insulation, setting clearances, balancing rotors, and completing no-load and load tests before delivery.
Motors, generators, power tools, and parts

BLS projects employment growth of 3% from 2024 to 2034 (BLS OOH, 2026). Automation equipment, electric vehicles, and appliance service increase the number of motor-based systems. More equipment means sustained repair demand. The field is fragmented, and advancement depends on accumulated skill. Younger workers are leaving, making strong technicians scarcer and improving prospects for those who stay.

According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), about 17,100 electric motor and power tool repairers were employed in 2024. Employment is projected to reach 17,700 by 2034, a net increase of about 600 jobs, with about 1,700 openings each year. Median annual pay was about $54,000 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace Electric Motor, Power Tool, And Related Repairers. Their core work involves dismantling, assembling, and testing physical equipment. Robots cannot perform this dirty, demanding, precise work economically in the near term. AI can provide diagnostic knowledge, parts specifications, and test-data records. These tools make technicians faster but cannot replace skilled hands and ears.

paragraphs: A score of 4/10 places this occupation in the low-moderate AI exposure range. The work produces repaired physical equipment. AI assists with information lookup and recordkeeping, while hands-on skill remains central and limits automation.

Low-moderate exposure does not mean standing still. Technicians who use intelligent test tools and record repair data work more efficiently and justify estimates more convincingly. As equipment becomes smarter, technicians who can repair intelligent systems become more valuable.

For a student with strong practical ability and patience, a vocational electromechanical program offers a practical path. A bachelor's degree is not the only route. Skills gain value after several years of apprenticeship, but safety and occupational health deserve close attention.

Move toward advanced equipment such as variable-frequency drives, servo motors, and electric vehicle motors. Few technicians can repair them, so service rates are higher. Use test instruments well and combine experience with data.

People with electrical fundamentals or appliance repair experience can transition quickly. Start as an apprentice in a repair shop or factory equipment department and earn credentials while working. In interviews, emphasize equipment types and fault cases rather than education alone.

Strong technicians are hard to recruit and retain. Pay by technical grade + piece rate so better craft earns visibly higher income. Provide proper workstations, tools, and protective equipment. Respect keeps skilled repairers on the job.

Digitalization in China's repair industry still centers on order and inventory management, while AI diagnostic tools are at an early stage. New-energy and automation equipment repair technicians are in clear shortage, and traditional motor repair shops face an aging workforce.
Major employers in China include motor repair shops, factory equipment maintenance departments, appliance and tool service centers, and equipment dealer service locations.

Motor repair abroad also depends on skilled workmanship, and demand remains stable as industrial automation spreads. Technicians with international electrical credentials, including IEC-system qualifications, are more competitive on overseas projects. Repair professionals with foreign-language skills are scarce.

Electric Motor, Power Tool, And Related Repairers work in repair workshops, factory equipment departments, tool repair shops, and service centers. They diagnose, dismantle, wind, repair, replace parts, and test motors, power tools, generators, and related equipment.
Median wage and employment projections from BLS OOH; wage distribution from BLS OES 2025 (collected 2026)
If you enjoy restoring broken equipment, this career offers that satisfaction every day. A customer's simple praise after collecting a repaired motor provides a tangible reward.

The appeal of this trade is that experience gains value over time. A veteran who has repaired motors for decades can identify a fault by sound, a skill no book can teach. Repairers also have durable demand because machines break and someone must fix them.
For people who enjoy hands-on work and do not mind grease, this trade offers confidence in a valuable skill and a dependable livelihood.

paragraphs: The greatest risks are wear on the body and erosion of skills, not AI. Machines keep getting newer while repairers age. Protecting your health is the starting lesson.

The greatest risks are physical strain and safety, not AI. Long periods of standing, heavy lifting, and contact with rotating equipment can injure the back and hands. The fragmented industry and low pay ceilings in small shops also limit income. Higher earnings depend on technical grade and reputation.

Electricians mainly install wiring, distribute power, and perform routine electrical maintenance, often on construction sites or in buildings. Motor repairers specialize in dismantling, winding, and testing motors, usually in workshops. Workers can move between the fields, but the emphasis differs.
